answer: Each identity deposits one original painting: a willow charcoal sketch finished with a self-mixed pigment wash of an ocean scene, its recipe hash-committed beforehand. The registry photographs it, stores a perceptual hash, and spot-checks 10% by panel; any work over 0.92 similarity to a prior deposit is refused and its $25 deposit fee is kept. One painting costs about $30 in materials plus 6 skilled hours, so 1,000 Sybils need $55,000 and 6,000 hours, and model-generated batches cluster and fail similarity. Trade-off: judging is partly subjective and trained painters are favoured.
